relations.rationale: Fay older than Ben and Ben older than Noor together establish an age order, but 13 alone about Fay-Ben doesn't determine Ben-Noor relation.
Fay's age relative to Ben has no bearing on Milo's work speed.
Fay's age relative to Ben has no bearing on the location of Ben's apartment.
Bringing her own tools doesn't imply anything about willingness to lend them out; these are independent behaviors.
Standing a head taller than most others directly explains why Noor is easy to spot in a crowd.
Noor's visibility in a crowd has no bearing on age comparisons between Ben and Noor.
Ben's age relative to Noor has no bearing on whether pieces made in class differ from each other.
Finishing pieces faster than others directly explains why Milo moves on to trimming while others are still shaping.
Milo moving to trimming faster is a minor detail unrelated to the aggregate outcome that shelves are lined with fired pieces by term's end.
Both describe activities during the break, suggesting they occur together as part of the same social time, supporting co-occurrence.
Laughing about pottery mishaps during break has no bearing on the location of Ben's apartment.
Ben's apartment being closest to the studio directly supports the claim that it's a short walk down the block from the studio.
Fay sketching varied glaze ideas beforehand could contribute to variation in finished pieces, weakly supporting the claim that each piece differs.
A shelf lined with many different types of pieces (mugs, bowls, vases) supports the claim that each piece is a little different from the last.
